title: U.S. and China Roll Back $30 Billion in Tariffs Following High-Stakes Washington Summit
snippet: President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed to slash tariffs on $30 billion worth of goods, launch talks on 'super intelligence,' and form a new trade council after three days of talks in Washington.
content:
WASHINGTON — The United States and China have agreed to slash tariffs on $30 billion worth of bilateral goods and open a formal dialogue on advanced artificial intelligence, following a three-day summit in Washington between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

According to a White House statement issued Friday, the consensus grants preferential tariff treatment for non-sensitive goods on both sides. American agricultural exports, timber, and cosmetics will benefit from lower rates, while U.S. imports of Chinese small appliances, toys, and household decorations will also see reduced duties.

Pragmatic Progress on Economic Relations

While the summit highlighted direct leadership engagement rather than a comprehensive economic overhaul, the agreement provides tangible relief for importers and exporters. Chinese Foreign Ministry officials noted that the two nations will establish a joint trade council to build on previous discussions held in Kuala Lumpur.

The agreement comes on the heels of a two-month extension to a trade truce originally scheduled to expire November 10. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted earlier this week that the extension offers critical breathing room for officials to negotiate a potential long-term trade framework.

Dialogue on Technology and Global Security

Technology policy also took center stage, with both governments agreeing to launch bilateral talks regarding the risks and rewards of artificial intelligence—notably agreeing to frame future discussions around the concept of 'super intelligence.' The next round of discussions is slated for November, accompanied by a dedicated communication channel for tech-related incidents.

Geopolitically, the two world leaders reaffirmed that Iran must fulfill its promise to refrain from developing nuclear weapons and agreed that no nation should levy transit tolls on international waterways. Both leaders also committed to supporting each other in hosting upcoming APEC and G20 summits.
